newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan police arrest Bhutto's aide.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan police arrest Bhutto's aide.

text.p: Pakistani police on Tuesday arrested ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's political secretary Naheed Khan, a spokesman for Bhutto said.
He said officers from the Federal Investigation Agency picked up Naheed at Islamabad airport as she arrived with Bhutto from the southern city of Karachi. It was not clear where she was headed.
There was no immediate information about the charges against Naheed or police comment on the arrest.

The arrest is the latest in a series after President Farooq Leghari dissolved the lower house of parliament and sacked Bhutto's three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.

Bhutto's spokesman, Shah Mahmoud Qureshi, said Naheed had been detained under a Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, the same law authorities have used to detain Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari since November 5.
The spokesman did not know how long Naheed would be held.
Other people already arrested include Nawaz Khokhar, the former science and technology minister, intelligence bureau chief Masood Sharif and several other government officials.
Bhutto has challenged the detention of Zardari, who was also investment minister in her cabinet, before Lahore High Court in Punjab province.

On Monday, police arrested Rifaat Askari, the former chairman of the state-run Oil and Gas Development Corporation, in connection with suspected irregularities in the award of a contract for building a dehydration plant at Uch oilfield in Punjab province, the official APP news agency said on Tuesday.
